config.title: Debounced Search

intro.title: Debounced Search
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a search input component that fetches and displays matching results from a mock API as the user types. You will learn how to implement debouncing, a technique that delays the execution of a function (like an API call) until after a user has stopped typing for a short period, preventing excessive requests and improving performance. The main technologies and constructs involved are Vue's reactive state with the ref function, the watch or watchEffect API to observe input changes, and a debounce utility to control the timing of the search. This approach ensures a smoother, more efficient user experience in real-time search interfaces.
intro.usecase: Debounced search is essential in modern web applications where real-time filtering improves user experience without overwhelming servers. You'll see this pattern in e-commerce search bars that suggest products as you type, dashboard data tables that filter results instantly, and admin panels with live filtering of user lists. As a Vue developer, implementing debounced search prevents excessive API calls while maintaining responsive interfaces, balancing performance with immediate feedback. This technique is crucial for search-heavy applications like customer support portals, analytics dashboards, and content management systems where users expect fast, filtered results.

objectives: Implement a reactive search query state in a Vue component
Construct a debounced function using Vue's watchEffect or composables
Bind the search input to the reactive query state with v-model
Configure the debounce delay to control API call frequency
Integrate the debounced search with a mock API or data filtering function
Render filtered results based on the debounced search query
Manipulate loading states during the debounced search execution

steps.title: Create the debounce function

steps.hint: The debounce function should use setTimeout to delay execution and clearTimeout to cancel pending executions when called again within the delay period.
steps.expectedOutcome: A debounce function is implemented inside the component's setup function, ready to be used with the search handler.
successCriteria: The debounce function is defined with parameters for callback and delay, uses setTimeout and clearTimeout, and returns a debounced function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the debounce function, but make sure it takes callback and delay parameters, uses setTimeout/clearTimeout, and returns a debounced function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The debounce function isn't implemented correctly. Review the example: it should accept a callback and delay, manage a timeout, and return a debounced version.
